purpose: Defines the local-first SQLite persistence layer, WAL concurrency mode, idempotent schema setup, connection pooling, repository APIs, and typed read models for Lumen session intelligence.
scope: Covers crates/lumen-store: SqliteStore, MigrationManager, QueueRepository, SessionRepository, ToolCallRepository, CommandEventRepository, FindingsRepository, RollupRepository, SnapshotRepository, TokenUsageRepository, and typed read models.
non_goals: Hook process interception or daemon async scheduling (handled by lumen-daemon).
Log file parsing or stream transformation (handled by lumen-session).
Direct network I/O or remote cloud sync.

Versioned schema migration chains or a versioned wire read-contract (ReadContractEnvelope/contract_version/JSON schema): pre-release, there is no installed base or external consumer to preserve compatibility for. MigrationManager applies one idempotent current-schema script instead of a versioned chain; revisit a versioned migration/wire-contract approach only once a real release or external consumer exists.
Category-score computation and discovered-category clustering (handled by lumen-insights, not yet integrated into any daemon transaction).

api_surface.name: SqliteStore
api_surface.signature: pub struct SqliteStore { pool: r2d2::Pool<r2d2_sqlite::SqliteConnectionManager>, is_read_only: bool }; impl SqliteStore { pub fn open(path: &Utf8Path) -> Result<Self, StoreError>; pub fn open_read_only(path: &Utf8Path) -> Result<Self, StoreError>; pub fn run_migrations(&self) -> Result<(), StoreError>; pub fn connection(&self) -> Result<r2d2::PooledConnection<r2d2_sqlite::SqliteConnectionManager>, StoreError>; }
api_surface.description: Connection pool manager configuring SQLite in WAL mode with PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON and query_only flags for concurrent multi-reader access. run_migrations applies MigrationManager's single idempotent current-schema script (safe to call on every open, not a versioned chain -- see non_goals).
error_conditions: StoreError::MigrationFailed if the schema setup script encounters a SQL error
StoreError::ReadOnlyViolation if write query is attempted on read-only pool

api_surface.name: QueueRepository
api_surface.signature: pub struct QueueRepository<'a> { conn: &'a rusqlite::Connection }; impl<'a> QueueRepository<'a> { pub fn enqueue(&self, provider: &str, session_id: &str, source_path: &str, source_hash: u64) -> Result<i64, StoreError>; pub fn fetch_pending(&self, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<QueuedSessionRow>, StoreError>; pub fn mark_completed(&self, id: i64) -> Result<(), StoreError>; pub fn mark_failed(&self, id: i64, error: &str) -> Result<(), StoreError>; }
api_surface.description: Repository managing the ingestion_queue table with exponential retry scheduling and dead-letter classification after 3 failures.

api_surface.name: SessionRepository
api_surface.signature: pub struct SessionRepository<'a> { conn: &'a rusqlite::Connection }; impl<'a> SessionRepository<'a> { pub fn upsert_session(&self, record: &SessionFactRecord) -> Result<(), StoreError>; pub fn get_session(&self, provider: &str, id: &str) -> Result<Option<SessionDetailReadModel>, StoreError>; pub fn list_recent(&self, filter: &SessionFilter) -> Result<Vec<SessionSummaryReadModel>, StoreError>; }
api_surface.description: Repository for normalized session facts, supporting idempotent upserts keyed on (provider, provider_session_id) and typed read models. get_session requires a provider parameter because the sessions table's real uniqueness constraint is UNIQUE(provider, provider_session_id) -- a session is only truly identified by the pair, not by provider_session_id alone. A provider_session_id-only lookup can theoretically resolve the wrong row if two different providers happen to report an identical session id.

api_surface.name: FindingsRepository
api_surface.signature: pub struct FindingsRepository<'a> { conn: &'a rusqlite::Connection }; impl<'a> FindingsRepository<'a> { pub fn insert_findings(&self, session_id: &str, findings: &[FindingFactRecord]) -> Result<(), StoreError>; pub fn list_top_findings(&self, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<FindingReadModel>, StoreError>; }
api_surface.description: Repository storing structured findings with confidence scores, evidence JSON payloads, and rule versions.

api_surface.name: ToolCallRepository
api_surface.signature: pub struct ToolCallRepository<'a> { conn: &'a rusqlite::Connection }; impl<'a> ToolCallRepository<'a> { pub fn new(conn: &'a rusqlite::Connection) -> Self; pub fn insert_tool_calls(&self, session_id: i64, calls: &[ToolCallFactRecord]) -> Result<(), StoreError>; pub fn list_by_session(&self, session_id: i64) -> Result<Vec<ToolCallReadModel>, StoreError>; pub fn tool_counts_by_session(&self, session_id: i64) -> Result<BTreeMap<CompactString, usize>, StoreError>; pub fn error_counts_by_session(&self, session_id: i64) -> Result<BTreeMap<CompactString, usize>, StoreError>; }
api_surface.description: Repository for the tool_calls table (id, session_id, turn_index, tool_name, call_id, intent_kind, is_error, latency_ms). insert_tool_calls batch-inserts ToolCallFactRecord rows for a session using a single prepared statement in a loop, following FindingsRepository::insert_findings's pattern; an empty slice inserts zero rows without error. tool_counts_by_session and error_counts_by_session are the methods SessionRepository::get_session uses to populate SessionDetailReadModel's tool_counts/error_counts fields (previously hardcoded to BTreeMap::new()).

api_surface.name: RollupRepository
api_surface.signature: pub struct RollupRepository<'a> { conn: &'a rusqlite::Connection }; impl<'a> RollupRepository<'a> { pub fn new(conn: &'a rusqlite::Connection) -> Self; pub fn upsert_rollup(&self, record: &RollupFactRecord) -> Result<(), StoreError>; pub fn get_rollup(&self, period_start: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>, period_type: &str) -> Result<Option<RollupReadModel>, StoreError>; pub fn list_rollups(&self, period_type: &str, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<RollupReadModel>, StoreError>; }
api_surface.description: Repository for the rollups table (id, period_start, period_type, session_count, total_cost_usd, total_savings_usd, total_duration_ms). upsert_rollup's idempotent ON CONFLICT requires the CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_rollups_period ON rollups(period_start, period_type) statement in MigrationManager::SCHEMA.

api_surface.name: CommandEventRepository
api_surface.signature: pub struct CommandEventRepository<'a> { conn: &'a rusqlite::Connection }; impl<'a> CommandEventRepository<'a> { pub fn new(conn: &'a rusqlite::Connection) -> Self; pub fn insert_command_events(&self, provider: &str, session_id: &str, events: &[CommandEventFactRecord]) -> Result<(), StoreError>; pub fn list_by_session(&self, provider: &str, session_id: &str) -> Result<Vec<CommandEventReadModel>, StoreError>; }
api_surface.description: Repository for the command_events table. insert_command_events persists command_base and redacted argument patterns per CRIT-LUMEN-037's redaction requirement, ensuring zero raw private arguments are written. Both methods require a provider parameter because the sessions table's real uniqueness constraint is UNIQUE(provider, provider_session_id) -- a session is only truly identified by the pair, not by provider_session_id alone. A provider_session_id-only lookup can theoretically resolve the wrong row if two different providers happen to report an identical session id.

api_surface.name: SnapshotRepository
api_surface.signature: pub struct SnapshotRepository<'a> { conn: &'a rusqlite::Connection }; impl<'a> SnapshotRepository<'a> { pub fn new(conn: &'a rusqlite::Connection) -> Self; pub fn save_snapshot(&self, provider: &str, session_id: &str, data: &[u8]) -> Result<i64, StoreError>; pub fn get_latest_snapshot(&self, provider: &str, session_id: &str) -> Result<Option<Vec<u8>>, StoreError>; }
api_surface.description: Repository for the session_snapshots table (created by MigrationManager::SCHEMA per CRIT-LUMEN-032 but previously unimplemented). Used by lumen-daemon's PreCompact hook handler to persist pre-compaction transcript BLOBs.
error_conditions: StoreError::WriteFailed if the BLOB insert fails or exceeds configured size limits

api_surface.name: TokenUsageRepository
api_surface.signature: pub struct TokenUsageRepository<'a> { conn: &'a rusqlite::Connection }; impl<'a> TokenUsageRepository<'a> { pub fn new(conn: &'a rusqlite::Connection) -> Self; pub fn insert_token_usage(&self, provider: &str, session_id: &str, economics: &lumen_model::TokenEconomics) -> Result<(), StoreError>; }
api_surface.description: Repository for the token_usage table (created by MigrationManager::SCHEMA per CRIT-LUMEN-032). insert_token_usage inserts one row per entry in TokenEconomics.per_model (keyed by model name, using ModelTokenSummary's input_tokens/output_tokens/cache_creation_tokens/cache_read_tokens/cost_usd/turns fields directly) rather than an invented intermediate record type. Requires a provider parameter because the sessions table's real uniqueness constraint is UNIQUE(provider, provider_session_id) -- a session is only truly identified by the pair, not by provider_session_id alone. A provider_session_id-only lookup can theoretically resolve the wrong row if two different providers happen to report an identical session id.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: WHEN SqliteStore opens a database file, THE SYSTEM SHALL configure PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL and PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON.
WHEN open_read_only is called, THE SYSTEM SHALL configure PRAGMA query_only = ON and disallow any INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE operations.

WHEN MigrationManager::SCHEMA is applied to a fresh database, THE SYSTEM SHALL create ingestion_queue, session_snapshots, pipeline_runs, sessions, tool_calls, command_events, token_usage (including its turns column), session_category_scores, findings, rollups (including the ux_rollups_period unique index per CRIT-LUMEN-120), and discovered_categories tables. This is one idempotent script, not a versioned migration chain -- see the spec's non_goals.
WHEN upsert_session is called multiple times with identical (provider, provider_session_id), THE SYSTEM SHALL perform an idempotent update without creating duplicate rows.
WHEN mark_failed is invoked on an ingestion queue item whose retry_count reaches 3, THE SYSTEM SHALL transition its status to 'dead_letter' and record the last error string.
IF MigrationManager::SCHEMA fails to apply, THE SYSTEM SHALL roll back the transaction and return StoreError::MigrationFailed without modifying database state.
WHEN list_recent is executed with limit = 50, THE SYSTEM SHALL return typed SessionSummaryReadModel structs in under 2 milliseconds.

WHEN command events are inserted, THE SYSTEM SHALL store command_base and redacted argument patterns, ensuring zero raw private arguments are persisted. Redaction determines what to redact by the SHAPE of the token's value (entropy-based secret detection, the model used by gitleaks/ripsecrets/trufflehog -- a token is flagged as a likely secret when its character-diversity makes random occurrence implausible, or it matches a known secret-prefix allowlist, regardless of whether it starts with '-'), not by CLI-parsing position. Flag NAMES (not values) remain safe to preserve verbatim, consistent with Langfuse's documented masking approach (structure-preserving redaction, not whole-text scrubbing).
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: FIXED 2026-08-22: redact_args (command_event.rs) now tokenizes with the shlex crate (real shell-word splitting, falling back to a whitespace split only if the input isn't valid shell syntax) and redacts by shape via shannon_entropy + a SECRET_PREFIXES allowlist (sk-, ghp_, xox, AKIA, etc.), instead of the prior 'starts with a single -' heuristic. Reproduced and verified fixed against both real inputs named in the original finding ('--api-key -sk-live-abc123SECRET' and 'mysql -pMySecretPassword123') plus a quoted-multiword-argument case proving the shlex tokenization fix. Prior art: shlex/shell-words (docs.rs) for tokenization, gitleaks/ripsecrets' entropy-based approach for the redaction signal.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: IF a database is locked by a concurrent reader, THE SYSTEM SHALL retry with busy_timeout = 5000ms before returning an error.

WHEN insert_tool_calls is called with a non-empty slice of ToolCallFactRecord, THE SYSTEM SHALL insert one row per record into tool_calls for the given session_id using a single prepared statement, and an empty slice SHALL insert zero rows without error.

WHEN tool_counts_by_session or error_counts_by_session is called for a session_id, THE SYSTEM SHALL return a BTreeMap keyed by tool_name whose values equal, respectively, the total count of tool_calls rows and the count of tool_calls rows with is_error = true for that session_id.

WHEN SessionRepository::get_session populates SessionDetailReadModel's tool_counts and error_counts fields, THE SYSTEM SHALL invoke tool_counts_by_session(id) / error_counts_by_session(id) using the internal integer sessions.id already returned by its row query, not the session_id: &str input parameter.

WHEN upsert_rollup is called multiple times with a RollupFactRecord sharing identical (period_start, period_type), THE SYSTEM SHALL perform an idempotent update without creating duplicate rows, backed by CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_rollups_period ON rollups(period_start, period_type) in MigrationManager::SCHEMA.
WHEN get_rollup is called with a (period_start, period_type) pair that has no matching row, THE SYSTEM SHALL return Ok(None) rather than an error.
WHEN list_rollups is called with a given period_type and limit, THE SYSTEM SHALL return at most `limit` RollupReadModel structs whose period_type matches, ordered by period_start descending.

WHEN insert_command_events is called with a non-empty slice of CommandEventFactRecord, THE SYSTEM SHALL insert one row per record into command_events for the given session_id, persisting only command_base and redacted argument patterns per CRIT-LUMEN-037.

WHEN save_snapshot is called, THE SYSTEM SHALL insert the BLOB into session_snapshots and return its row id, and get_latest_snapshot SHALL return the most recently inserted BLOB for the given (provider, session_id) or None if none exists.

WHEN insert_token_usage is called with a TokenEconomics value, THE SYSTEM SHALL insert one token_usage row per entry in TokenEconomics.per_model, using that entry's ModelTokenSummary fields directly (no intermediate record type).

FIXED 2026-08-23 (found during CRIT-LUMEN-171's implementation). WHEN a session is persisted via upsert_session and later read back via list_recent or get_session, THE SYSTEM SHALL return the same TokenEconomics.is_fully_priced value the session was ingested with, for both the session-level value (SessionSummaryReadModel.is_fully_priced, sessions.is_fully_priced column) and the per-model breakdown (ModelTokenSummary.is_fully_priced, token_usage.is_fully_priced column) -- never a hardcoded true regardless of the real value.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Real bug found while surveying CRIT-LUMEN-171's call sites (2026-08-23): is_fully_priced had no backing column in either the sessions or token_usage table at all -- upsert_session/insert_token_usage never wrote it, and get_session/per_model_by_session hardcoded is_fully_priced: true in the reconstructed TokenEconomics/ModelTokenSummary regardless of the real value, both marked inline as 'not yet a persisted column -- pre-existing read-back gap'. list_recent's SessionSummaryReadModel didn't carry the field at all, so lumen-cli's `sessions` table read s.total_cost_usd with no is_fully_priced check whatsoever (crates/lumen-cli/src/main.rs) -- a genuinely unpriced session (unrecognized model) round-tripped through the store and displayed as an indistinguishable-from-real $0.0000 everywhere the store's read models were used, the exact CRIT-LUMEN-008 bug class this project has repeatedly fixed at the adapter layer, manifesting instead at the persistence layer. Fixed by adding is_fully_priced INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 to both tables' CREATE TABLE statements (MigrationManager::SCHEMA), persisting/reading it in both repositories, adding it to SessionSummaryReadModel, and fixing lumen-cli's `sessions` command to use the new Cost-based accessor (CRIT-LUMEN-171) instead of reading total_cost_usd directly. Regression test: test_session_repository_is_fully_priced_round_trips_through_store.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: RESOLVED 2026-08-23 with a split decision, one repository per option named in this criterion's original text. (a) ToolCallRepository IS NOW wired into lumen-cli: SessionFactRecord gained a tool_calls: Vec<ToolCallFactRecord> field, and SessionRepository::upsert_session persists it (idempotently, via ToolCallRepository::delete_for_session + insert_tool_calls, the same pattern already used for token_usage) -- cmd_ingest builds it from CanonicalTranscript.turns, which already carries the real tool-call data. (b) CommandEventRepository, FindingsRepository, QueueRepository, RollupRepository, and SnapshotRepository remain deliberately unwired, each for a distinct, now-documented reason (see reasoning) -- none is simply forgotten.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Audit finding (2026-08-22, adversarially verified): unlike lumen-analysis's RawMessageAccumulators, which carry a documented rationale for their exclusion from AnalyticsEngine, nothing explained why these six repositories existed unconsumed. Investigating concretely (2026-08-23) found ToolCallRepository was a materially different case from the other five: its READ side (tool_counts_by_session/error_counts_by_session) was already wired into SessionRepository::get_session and already shipped in SessionDetailReadModel's serialized/CLI output -- so tool_counts/error_counts were an already-advertised feature that silently always returned empty for every real session, not merely an unbuilt one. Wiring its write side was a real but bounded fix (the data already exists on CanonicalTranscript; the only new judgment calls were an intent_kind string mapping, defaulting an unmatched call's is_error to false, and approximating per-call latency_ms from the owning turn's total, all documented inline). The other five have no such existing read-side promise and each needs real, distinct new feature work with no existing caller to build from: FindingsRepository needs a rule/detection engine that doesn't exist yet (nothing computes a Finding from a real session today); QueueRepository and SnapshotRepository are for async/incremental ingestion and already explicitly reserved for a future lumen-daemon consumer (SPEC-LUMEN-004-DAEMON.json); RollupRepository needs a period-aggregation job that doesn't exist yet (nothing calls upsert_rollup in production either); CommandEventRepository needs real shell-command extraction from ToolIntent (its variants -- VersionControl{action}, TestExecution{runner}, Other{raw_name} -- don't cleanly decompose into CommandEventFactRecord's command_base + sanitized_args shape the way tool-call data cleanly decomposed into ToolCallFactRecord). Building any of these five now would be speculative feature work with no demonstrated need, the exact pattern this project already reversed once this session (see the ReadContractEnvelope/versioned-migration-chain build-then-revert, commits 0433201/b6a5f67/4176a77) -- deferred, not resolved by building, consistent with that standing lesson.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: FIXED 2026-08-23. WHEN SessionRepository::upsert_session persists a session's row plus its token_usage and tool_calls sub-records, THE SYSTEM SHALL commit all of them as one atomic transaction (via Connection::unchecked_transaction), NOT as separate autocommit statements -- a crash or error partway through must never leave the session row updated while its sub-records are only partially deleted/inserted.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: Full-codebase performance/correctness review finding (2026-08-23): upsert_session performed 1 (session upsert) + 1 (select-back) + up to N (token_usage delete+insert) + up to M (tool_calls delete+insert) separate statements under SQLite's default autocommit, each its own commit -- a session with many tool calls did dozens of independent commits instead of one, and a crash or error mid-sequence left the session row updated with sub-records in an inconsistent partial state. Fixed by wrapping the whole sequence in one transaction. unchecked_transaction (rather than requiring Connection::transaction's &mut Connection) was a judgment call: SessionRepository, like every repository in this crate, is constructed from a shared &Connection so callers can freely construct multiple repositories against the same connection in the same scope -- switching to &mut Connection would be a larger, cross-cutting signature change to every repository constructor for a fix scoped to this one method. unchecked_transaction is documented by rusqlite specifically for this shared-reference scenario; SQLite itself has no issue beginning a transaction without exclusive Rust-level mutable access. Regression: all 35 existing lumen-store tests (including the multithreaded concurrency test) continue to pass unchanged, confirming no behavioral regression; a dedicated crash-mid-transaction fault-injection test was considered but not added -- SQLite's transaction atomicity is a foundational, independently-tested guarantee, not custom logic this codebase is re-implementing, so the existing round-trip tests are the right level of coverage here.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: FIXED 2026-08-24. WHEN a session is read back via list_recent or get_session, THE SYSTEM SHALL return the same has_anomalies value the session was ingested with (SessionSummaryReadModel.has_anomalies, sessions.has_anomalies column), NOT silently omit it -- lumen-cli's `sessions`/`session` commands SHALL display it.
acceptance_criteria.reasoning: CRIT-LUMEN-179 wired real anomaly detection and upsert_session already persisted has_anomalies (since CRIT-LUMEN-174), but SessionSummaryReadModel never carried the field at all, and list_recent/get_session never selected the column back out of sessions -- a real, already-working detector's result was unreachable from `lumen sessions`/`lumen session` regardless. Fixed by adding has_anomalies to SessionSummaryReadModel, selecting it in both queries, and adding an Anomalies column/line to the CLI's table and detail output. Regression test: test_session_repository_has_anomalies_round_trips_through_store (crates/lumen-store/tests/test_store.rs), covering both a session with a real detected anomaly and a clean session with none.

reasoning: Establishes the durable, local-first SQLite WAL storage engine, schema setup, repository boundaries, and typed read models. Revised 2026-08-22: the versioned migration chain (previously V1-V7, with per-version tracking in a schema_migrations table) was replaced with MigrationManager applying one idempotent current-schema script, and CRIT-LUMEN-038 (ReadContractEnvelope/contract_version/schemas/read-contracts/v1.schema.json) was removed entirely -- both were versioning/compatibility infrastructure built for a production installed base and an external consumer (a hypothetical future Mac app) that don't exist yet, on a project with zero releases. Pre-release, changing a column or table just means editing MigrationManager::SCHEMA directly; a local dev database that predates the change is safe to delete and let recreate, since there is no real user data anywhere that needs to survive a schema change. Revisit versioned migrations and a wire read-contract once a real release or a real external consumer exists -- see non_goals.
